generation.text:
In my sophomore year of high school, I had a part-time job delivering newspapers to subscribers in our town. One morning, I was running a bit late and decided to skip a few driveways to meet my paper's deadline. As I rushed through a cul-de-sac, I failed to notice an elderly woman's dog had ventured out onto the road. My motorized newspaper bike was silent, and I was moving fast. I swerved sharply to avoid the dog, but the bike's kickstand caught on the dog's leash, flipping me and the bike over in a loud crash. I was embarrassed and sore, but no one was hurt. 

My boss was understanding and let me catch up on the missing driveways the next day. The experience made me realize the importance of not cutting corners and always paying attention, no matter how minor
